meetings.headline: Committee to fast-track a stalled hire's job review and plans SAP bylaw changes on voting and access
meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Personnel Committee met with the town manager, HR director and labor counsel to clarify its role under the SAP bylaw, focusing on a job-description review that was delaying the posting of a vacant part-time data collector position. The committee agreed to hold a Thursday Zoom meeting to clear that posting, and discussed possible future bylaw amendments -- exempting recently-reviewed job descriptions, using executive session for above-step-four pay decisions, and changing the three-member unanimous vote requirement to a majority -- to be brought as warrant articles, with a classification/compensation study proposed for future town-meeting funding.

budget_items.what_was_said: Labor counsel described the vacant position as a part-time, 19-an-hour, weekly-hours role critical to office administrative functions, used to illustrate delay caused by mandatory job-description review.

The committee discussed seeking preliminary quotes from consultants for a comp/classification study and putting a placeholder warrant article through November town meeting, contingent on free cash being certified; the study would likely begin work informing FY29.

budget_items.topic: Requests for starting pay above step four
budget_items.what_was_said: Counsel explained that if the town manager wants to start a new hire above step four of the pay scale, the request goes to the full committee rather than being decided unilaterally, potentially in executive session.

decisions.decision: Committee will hold a special Zoom meeting on Thursday to review the data collector job description so it can be posted after the meeting.
Chair will draft and send the agenda for the Thursday meeting; HR will forward the job description and any comparables in advance by email.

Committee will consider a future SAP bylaw amendment exempting job descriptions reviewed and approved within a set prior period (e.g. two years) from re-review before posting, if there is no proposed change.
Committee leaning toward limiting mandatory reviews to full- and part-time staff positions, not recurring seasonal/call positions like call firefighters or library pages.
Committee agreed it will request executive session (citing strategy re: non-union personnel) when considering a hire above step four of the pay scale, rather than amending the bylaw for this.
Committee will consider amending the SAP bylaw so votes require a majority rather than unanimous three-in-the-affirmative.
Committee will place a placeholder warrant article (and formally vote at a future meeting before September 17) to reserve space for these bylaw changes and for salary/comp consulting funding.
The item to align SAP longevity provisions with collective bargaining agreements will be held for the spring town meeting discussion rather than acted on now.
Going forward HR/town manager will send job-description and related emails to the whole committee rather than one member, and members agreed not to use reply-all.

meetings.headline: Personnel Committee, unsure of its own authority, parsed the town attorney's new reading of its bylaws
meetings.summary: The Personnel Committee (a three-member board, not yet fully seated) spent nearly the whole meeting working through correspondence from town counsel Mark Terry interpreting the committee's bylaws — its role in job descriptions, wage/salary equity reviews, reclassifications, new-hire pay above minimum step, and department budget pay-adjustment sections — and repeatedly found the bylaw language unclear on where its authority actually begins and ends. No formal votes were taken on substance; the committee agreed to seek outside opinions on the bylaws, meet with the attorney, request personnel data from HR, and possibly amend the bylaws with a plainer mission statement at a future town meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The committee discussed a bylaw requirement to periodically review wage and salary schedules for equity, and debated whether an outside entity, HR, or the committee itself should conduct it. No such review appeared to have been done recently; the committee proposed doing it at least every three years and getting historical data on when it was last done.

The chair raised whether funds would need to be allocated, possibly via a special town meeting article, to pay an outside consultant to conduct the wage and salary review. No dollar figures were discussed; the group planned to ask the town attorney about timing and process.

The bylaw requires each department head to include a pay adjustment section in its annual budget request, with expenditures from it needing personnel board approval. The committee was unsure whether its role is to approve or merely review these sections and planned to seek clarification from the town attorney.

The bylaw requires the personnel committee to determine that a position reclassification is consistent with the salary administration plan before it proceeds, with the request ultimately needing a town meeting vote to fund. The committee discussed that a department head and HR bring the request forward, not the employee directly.

budget_items.topic: New hire pay above minimum step
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager must consult the committee chair before authorizing a new hire's pay above the minimum step of a grade range, and the full committee must vote if the hire is above step four. Discussion suggested such a vote could occur in executive session for privacy.

decisions.decision: The committee will discuss the attorney's bylaw letter section by section rather than reading it into the record.
The committee will compile a list of documents (job descriptions, employment contracts, current steps/grades) it wants access to on the shared drive, to raise with the town attorney and HR.
The chair will maintain a SharePoint folder for each SAP position containing its job description and related grade/salary information.
The next meeting (August 17) will focus on the chair's follow-up conversation with Attorney Mark Terry, who is expected to attend.

The committee will send HR Director Julie Belliveau a written request for a spreadsheet of all SAP-covered employees with grade/step, current job descriptions, anticipated new hires under the SAP, current collective bargaining agreements, and individual employment contracts, and will invite her to attend meetings.
The committee will keep meeting at the current lower Ritter conference room venue through the end of the year, revisiting accessible winter locations (library, town hall, DPW) later.

meetings.headline: Reactivated Personnel Committee elects officers, begins line-by-line review of the town's salary bylaws
meetings.summary: This was the first meeting of Lunenburg's Personnel Committee since it was reactivated after being inactive since 2024; the three appointed members elected officers and then read through the town's salary administration plan bylaw section by section, flagging language they want clarified by town counsel and the HR director. No formal policy changes were voted; the committee set a recurring meeting schedule and agreed to bring a list of questions to its next meeting on the 20th.

attendees.name_as_heard: Tanya Doll (also heard as Tanya Willard Doll)

budget_items.topic: Review of wage and salary schedules
budget_items.what_was_said: The bylaw requires the committee to review wage and salary schedules of all positions at a set interval and recommend action to the select board; members said comparable-town wage data has historically been hard to get accurately.

budget_items.topic: New hire starting pay / step approval
budget_items.what_was_said: New employees are to be hired at the minimum of the job's pay range unless the town manager, after consulting the chair, authorizes a higher step; the committee must formally vote to approve any new-hire pay above a stated step.

figures_as_heard: up to five days of vacation leave
budget_items.what_was_said: The plan lets the town manager offer recruitment incentives such as deposited vacation time or a sign-on bonus when hard-to-fill critical positions can't attract qualified applicants; the committee was unsure whether the town manager needs select board sign-off to use this.

Department heads must include a pay-adjustment section in their annual budget request, and any planned increase within the salary plan needs personnel committee approval before it goes into the budget; a member questioned whether step increases are actually automatic rather than discretionary.
Non-exempt employees get overtime at a stated multiplier of their regular rate for hours worked beyond a 40-hour week, counting paid leave time toward the 40 hours.

budget_items.topic: Compensatory time in lieu of overtime
budget_items.what_was_said: Employees may take compensatory time at the overtime rate instead of cash, but it must be used within a stated number of days.

Full-time employees accrue sick leave monthly up to a stated annual amount, cumulative up to a stated maximum, and it can be donated through a sick leave bank whose current status the committee was unsure of.

Employees who retire in good standing and were hired before a stated cutoff date get a percentage of accumulated unused sick leave paid out, rising with years of service; a member noted this only applies to employees hired before a certain date and few may still qualify.

budget_items.topic: Parental leave use of sick leave
budget_items.what_was_said: New parents may draw on a prorated cap of sick leave hours for parental leave.
Employees receive an annual longevity bonus as a percentage of salary starting after a stated years-of-service threshold, increasing at further milestones, paid each year on the anniversary date.

budget_items.topic: Pay upon transfer to a lower-graded job
budget_items.what_was_said: The committee discussed that an employee transferred to a lower-paying job could actually lose pay under the plan's placement formula, and planned to raise questions about it with counsel.

decisions.decision: Invite town counsel Attorney Terry and the HR director to the committee's next meeting (the 20th) to review bylaw language and roles.
Chair will ask the town's IT/facilities contact (Mason) about a portable meeting device (the 'owl') so meetings could move to other rooms.
Chair will compile a written list of the committee's questions for Attorney Terry and HR, to be sent ahead of the next meeting.
Committee will request copies of the recently finalized union contracts once available.
Committee will ask HR/town manager about the current status of the sick leave bank.
Committee will meet on the first and third Monday of each month going forward, and the chair will look into using the senior center or library as a more accessible meeting space.
Members will send any questions for Attorney Terry and HR to the chair by Monday the 13th so they can be answered in advance.
